home.heroText: For five generations, our watchmakers in the Vallée de Joux have assembled, bevelled and regulated every movement one by one. No two ORVANE watches are ever quite alike.
home.introTitle: We do not make watches. We make time that lasts.
home.introText: An ORVANE watch requires between 400 and 1,200 hours of work. Each piece bears the hallmark of the watchmaker who assembled it, and can be restored by our workshops forever.

movementSteps.title: The mainplate
movementSteps.text: The foundation of the movement, decorated by hand with perlage: 1,400 overlapping circles of perfect regularity.

movementSteps.title: The gear train
movementSteps.text: Four wheels carry the energy from the barrel. Every tooth is polished to reduce friction to the bare minimum.

movementSteps.title: The escapement
movementSteps.text: The balance oscillates 28,800 times an hour. Its hairspring is adjusted by hand in six positions and three temperatures.

movementSteps.title: The bridges
movementSteps.text: Bevelled at 45° and polished with gentian wood, they catch the light the way jewellery does.

home.craftText: Guillocheurs, enamellers, bevellers, setters, regulators: sixteen rare crafts follow one another on every watch. Some gestures can only be learned after ten years at the bench.

maison.title: Five generations, a single farmhouse
maison.intro: Founded in 1891 in Le Brassus by Auguste Orvane, the Maison has remained independent and family-owned. It has never moved its workshops.

values.title: Independence
values.text: Owned by the Orvane family since 1891, the Maison sets its own pace and only produces what it can master.

values.title: Transmission
values.text: Every apprentice is trained for four years by a master watchmaker. Knowledge passes from hand to hand.

values.title: Durability
values.text: Certified recycled gold and platinum, hydro-powered workshops, lifetime repairability guaranteed.

values.title: Discretion
values.text: No celebrities, no ostentatious logos. An ORVANE watch is recognised first by touch.

maison.quote: A watch must be able to outlive the one who made it, and the one who wore it.
maison.familyTitle: The Vallée de Joux, our only address
maison.familyText: At 1,000 metres above sea level, between Lac de Joux and the Risoud forest, 64 watchmakers work in the renovated farmhouse where it all began. The light is clear, the silence almost total.

craft.title: Slowness as a method
craft.intro: Between the first sketch and the delivery of a watch, sometimes two years go by. These are the steps that make an ORVANE.

steps.title: Drawing
steps.text: Every calibre begins as a 10:1 scale drawing, made by hand before any digital modelling.

steps.title: Machining
steps.text: Mainplates and bridges are machined to within 2 microns, then deburred by hand one by one.

steps.title: Decoration
steps.text: Perlage, Côtes de Genève, 45° bevelling, mirror polishing: up to 120 hours for a single movement.

steps.title: Assembly
steps.text: A single watchmaker assembles the movement from start to finish and stamps it with a personal hallmark.

steps.title: Regulation
steps.text: 21-day chronometric testing, in six positions and three temperatures.

steps.title: Casing
steps.text: The movement meets its case, dial and hands. A final water-resistance test, then the signature.

craft.compareText: Slide the handle: on the left, a raw bridge straight from machining; on the right, the same bridge after eleven hours of bevelling and polishing.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Can't find the answer? Our concierge replies Monday to Saturday.

items.q: Where can I buy an ORVANE watch?
items.a: Exclusively in our eight salons and through a few authorised retailers. We do not sell online, so that every watch is handed over in person and fitted to its owner's wrist.
All our watches come with an 8-year international warranty from the date of purchase, upon presentation of the digital warranty card.

items.q: How often should my watch be serviced?
items.a: We recommend a full service approximately every 7 years. An annual water-resistance check is advised for Abysse watches worn in water.

items.q: Can I commission a unique piece?
items.a: Yes. Our unique-piece workshop completes about ten commissions a year: engraving, painted enamel, personalised dial or bespoke complication. Allow 12 to 24 months.
Our workshops keep the plans of every calibre produced since 1891 and can remake a missing part identically.
Every movement is tested for 21 days in our workshops. The precious metals we use come from certified recycled sources.

items.q: How do I change the strap?
items.a: Our straps feature a quick-change system: a simple press on the spring bar is enough, no tools required.
